items.caption: 20 tiles in 4 groups of 5: divisible
items.text: Twenty tiles fill four complete rows of five with nothing left over, so 5 divides 20 and 20 = 5 · 4 with k = 4: the definition a | b drawn as a full rectangle. items.caption: 23 = 5 · 4 + 3: four full rows and three left over
items.text: The four complete rows are the quotient q = 4 and the three tiles that could not start a fifth row are the remainder r = 3, with 0 ≤ 3 < 5 exactly as the division algorithm requires. items.caption: The ÷4 column: every fourth number
items.text: The highlighted column marks every fourth number, and the marks depend only on the last two digits: 12, 16, 112 and 116 are all marked because 12 and 16 are multiples of 4, while the hundreds digit changes nothing. That is the rule for 4 as a column pattern. Check the last-two-digits rule against the column on the

items.caption: gcd(252, 105) = 21: the factor that reduces 105/252 to 5/12
items.text: Simplifying a fraction means dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor, and the algorithm finds it without factoring: 252 = 105 · 2 + 42, 105 = 42 · 2 + 21, 42 = 21 · 2, so the gcd is 21 and 105/252 = 5/12 in one step. items.caption: Six slots, six possible remainders: 0 to 5
items.text: The wheel has exactly six slots and every integer lands in one of them, so there are exactly six possible remainders mod 6, from 0 to 5, and none can equal 6 itself: that would be slot 0 again. The slots are the complete set of residues. Change the modulus and count the slots on the

items.caption: One slot holds 3, 9, 15, …: a congruence class
items.text: Every number that lands in the same slot shares the same remainder, and those numbers are congruent modulo 6: the slot is the congruence class, and 3 ≡ 9 ≡ 15 (mod 6) is the statement that they sit together. Congruence is equality of slots. Highlight a class and read its members on the

items.page: Modulo of Negative Numbers: Truncated vs Floored Division
items.caption: One class, many representatives
items.text: Every number in a slot is congruent to every other: −1 and 2 occupy the same slot mod 3 just as 3, 9 and 15 share a slot mod 6 here, so the two conventions’ answers, −1 and 2, are two names for one class. items.page: Modular Arithmetic: Operations, Power Cycles & Applications
items.caption: The playing field mod 6: slots 0 to 5
items.text: Every number, however large, is reduced to one of the six slots on the wheel, and every operation is carried out slot by slot: adding 4 to a number moves its slot four places round, and the result never leaves the wheel. items.text: Green 3 and its multiples from 9 up. Numbers divisible by both 2 and 3 — 12, 18, 24 and their kin — now wear both colors striped.

items.caption: mod 6, zero class pinned, frozen
items.text: The gold-edged slice holds 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36 — the multiples of 6, the only class where divisibility is true.
